meta.count_note: The paper text says 'six fault-injection tests' on Megatron-LM; the atom table has 7 rows because one is a control (a new file that should install).
meta.detail_note: `detail` on the Megatron rows is read by me from the atom's source ledger (one row per injected commit); the atom itself holds only the three columns.
meta.caveat: The t2-faults and t3 tables come from the paper's LiveLab build (2026-10-28). The conformance and PR tables come from the public repo's labs.

paper_megatron_fault_injection.title: Injected faults fail the way a restart would
paper_megatron_fault_injection.claim: Every injected fault fails or recovers as a restart would; none passes silently.
paper_megatron_fault_injection.setup: Megatron, one injected commit per fault. Correctness check: the first 40 training losses must match the reference.

rows.detail: rejected in 0.0 s with the file and line of the syntax error
check ended after 81.2 s with the injected RuntimeError; the next check of the base ran live
check ended after 96.2 s with the CUDA out-of-memory error; the next check of the base ran live
check ended after 82.2 s with the injected RuntimeError
the gate returned FAIL: 'missing or non-finite loss in steps 1-40'
installed live; loss matched the start; witness OK
the live process was lost during the check (66.4 s); the next check ran as a restart (270.4 s)

paper_kernel_fault_timing.title: Kernel faults: time to a failure
paper_kernel_fault_timing.setup: Attention prefill kernel (GQA), one GB200 GPU, compared with FlashInfer-Bench's own evaluator and with a restart

rows.observed: Live 2.2 s; restart 2.3 s; FlashInfer-Bench 418 s
Live 300 s + relaunch; restart 600 s; FlashInfer-Bench 717 s
rows.note: Hang times are set by timeouts (300 s live, 600 s restart).

rows.observed: Live: no result (a bug in the kernel worker); restart 5.0 s; FlashInfer-Bench 436 s

paper_kernel_fault_timing.known_bug: An illegal memory access currently returns no result in the live path.

repo_conformance_cases.setup: 2 layers, hidden 512, TP 2 on 2 GB200, deterministic mode, 2026-11-07; faults are real (a rank's process exits, a rank sleeps inside a train step)

cases.fault: A fault in the middle of an install (one participant fails after 2 of 3 swaps; another fails at commit)
cases.observed: both rolled back with `participant_failed`, base proven; control committed 3 targets

cases.fault: Unsupported edits: syntax error, changed closure, module constant, no code change
cases.expected: refuse with the right code, change nothing
cases.observed: `patch_invalid`, `closure_changed`, `outside_changes`, `empty_change`

cases.fault: Crash, hang, lost rank, tampered code
cases.expected: poison the session; respawn returns to base
cases.observed: each poisoned the lab; respawn 46.0 s (crash), 51.6 s (hang), 37.6 s (lost), 45.0 s (tamper)

cases.fault: Edit that never runs (an `MLP.__init__` edit)
cases.observed: proven False with `zero_witness` on both ranks; live loss stays at base, a fresh process differs

repo_pr_fault_receipts.setup: standby pool on B200 GPUs, Qwen3-8B (MoE model in brackets), under streaming load

cases.fault: Active engine killed (SIGKILL)
cases.observed: router saw a broken stream; first token from the other engine 29.8 ms after the fault (MoE 45.0 ms); output exact; leased respawn 30.6 s

cases.fault: Weights corrupted in the active holder
cases.expected: detect and fail over to a clean holder
cases.observed: digest mismatch on 1 tensor; first token 66.1 ms (MoE 134 ms); NCCL re-copy 55.7 ms, digest ok

cases.fault: Sticky CUDA error (device-side assert)
cases.observed: first token 32.0 ms (MoE 60.8 ms); leased respawn 29.8 s

cases.fault: Weight patch rejected by the gate
cases.expected: roll the patch back; never reach the standby or the ledger
cases.observed: 347 ms including apply and gate; holder restored byte for byte by NCCL re-copy (56.4 ms)
cases.note: Not run on the MoE model.

repo_pr_fault_receipts.note: 4931 streaming requests with 1 error (MoE: 5467 with 2), each a stream cut while the engine was being killed.

cases.fault: Quiesce timeout forced while rank 1 is inside its commit
cases.expected: host and every rank agree on rolled back
cases.observed: before the fix: host said rolled back but rank 1 kept the edit live (1692 launches). After: both ranks undone, base kernel text, tokens equal base

cases.fault: Edit to a Triton kernel that never launches on this GPU
cases.observed: before the fix: reported proven 1692/1692 (false). After: 0/0 with `zero_witness` on both ranks

cases.fault: Witness counter that fires on rank 0 only
cases.observed: before: proven True (counts summed). After: proven False, per-rank minimum 0

cases.fault: Engine stop when the port stays open
cases.observed: before: `stopped: true`. After: `stopped: false, port_open: true`, and nothing new starts

cases.fault: Live reconfigure the engine does not confirm
cases.observed: the report names the path (`in_process_live` or `restart`) with a restart reason
cases.note: The before/after table shows the old code reporting `restarted: false` while the engine still ran the old limit.

repo_pr_fault_receipts.setup: 2x B200, Qwen3-14B architecture TP 2, one zygote, three jobs, 30 checks all pass

cases.fault: Malformed requests to the zygote and the lab (3 each)
cases.observed: error events; ping and status still answer

cases.fault: Client times out or disconnects before its reply
cases.observed: rank 0 logged 4 gone clients; loss after the faults equal to before, bit for bit

cases.fault: Client disconnects during a job
cases.expected: stop the job and free the GPUs
cases.observed: all 8 processes gone and reaped in 18.6 s, GPU memory 0
cases.note: SIGTERM did not stop a rank waiting in a gloo round; it needed SIGKILL after the 10 s grace.

cases.fault: Zygote killed (SIGKILL) during a job
cases.observed: all 8 processes stopped in 0.05 s; GPU memory back to 0 within 60 s

cases.fault: `reset` with an extra or missing state key
cases.observed: `ok: false` naming the keys; covered by CPU cases; the GPU run shows the reset digest round trip equal on both ranks

related_drift_guard.fact: A live process that had installed 34 unrelated edits read up to 28% slow; a newly started one did not. The lab now relaunches a process that drifts more than 10%.
